CONTENT PREVIEW:
Feature: Separate liveness and readiness probes for DB health

# GitHub Issue #163: Separate liveness and readiness probes to prevent DB-induced CrashLoop

**Category**: improvement | **Scope**: Small

**Description**: Both the liveness and readiness probes on the `keystone-api` container currently use the same check: `HTTPGet /v3:5000`. This endpoint requires a working database connection — if MariaDB is temporarily unavailable, `/v3` returns HTTP 500, the liveness probe fails, and kubelet kills the container. With multiple replicas this creates a thundering-herd restart: all pods crash-loop simultaneously and bombard the recovering database with connection storms, delaying recovery further.

Separate the probes by intent:

- **Liveness probe** → `TCPSocket` on port 5000. This verifies that the uWSGI process is alive and accepting connections. A TCP check does not exercise the database path, so a transient DB outage will not trigger unnecessary restarts.
- **Readiness probe** → `HTTPGet /v3` on port 5000 (unchanged). This verifies full API functionality including database connectivity. When the DB is down, the pod becomes not-ready and is removed from the Service endpoints — no traffic is routed to it, but the process stays alive and can recover in-place once the DB returns.

<commit-best-practices>
<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0062): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>
